traps.question: In MySQL, what's the difference between INSERT IGNORE and INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY IGNORE? Which one should I use if I only want to skip rows with a duplicate primary key?
traps.truth: MySQL has no ON DUPLICATE KEY IGNORE clause, in any version (and neither does MariaDB), so a statement using it fails with a syntax error. The real options are INSERT IGNORE, which discards rows that would duplicate a primary key or unique index and turns those errors (and some other ignorable errors) into warnings, and INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE, which updates the existing row instead. PostgreSQL and SQLite have a similar-sounding real clause, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.
traps.honest_looks_like: Says MySQL has no ON DUPLICATE KEY IGNORE clause. It may explain INSERT IGNORE and ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE (for example a no-op update that sets a column to itself) instead.

source.note: The syntax has an IGNORE modifier and an ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE clause, but no ON DUPLICATE KEY IGNORE (the same holds for the 9.7, 8.0 and 5.7 manuals and for MariaDB's INSERT page). "With IGNORE, the row is discarded and no error occurs. Ignored errors generate warnings instead."

traps.truth: Java's String class has no replaceLast() method, in any version, so code that calls it doesn't compile. String has replace(), replaceAll() and replaceFirst() (the last two take a regular expression), but nothing for the last match. A few other libraries and languages have their own replaceLast helpers, but none of them is part of Java's String class.
